blocks.content: This topic consolidates exactly how a Pod actually reaches a Service's stable virtual IP, tying together the Services and Architecture modules' coverage of kube-proxy into one concrete, end-to-end picture.
1. Sending Traffic to a Virtual IP
blocks.text: 1. Sending Traffic to a Virtual IP

blocks.content: A Pod that wants to reach a backend, a database, an internal API, sends its traffic to that Service's virtual IP, exactly as covered in the Services module, unaware of, and unconcerned with, which real Pods are actually behind it.

blocks.alt: Traffic addressed to a stable virtual IP, not any specific real Pod

blocks.content: This is where kube-proxy, covered in the Architecture module, actually does its work, the rules it maintains on every node intercept traffic destined for a Service's virtual IP before it ever reaches anything real.

blocks.alt: The exact interception point where kube-proxy's rules take effect

blocks.content: 3. Redirected to a Real, Current Pod
blocks.text: 3. Redirected to a Real, Current Pod

blocks.content: kube-proxy redirects that traffic to one of the Service's actual backing Pods, drawn from the Endpoints list covered in the Services module, always the current, live set of matching Pods, never a stale or outdated one.

blocks.alt: Redirected to whichever real Pod is actually backing the Service right now

blocks.content: 4. Entirely Transparent to the Sending Pod
blocks.text: 4. Entirely Transparent to the Sending Pod

blocks.content: The Pod that initiated this request never sees any of this redirection happening, from its own point of view, it simply sent traffic to an address and got a response, the entire mechanism is invisible to it.

blocks.alt: A seamless illusion, the sending Pod has no idea any redirection occurred

blocks.content: 5. Exactly What Makes Service a Stable Abstraction
blocks.text: 5. Exactly What Makes Service a Stable Abstraction

blocks.content: This entire mechanism, virtual IP plus kube-proxy plus live Endpoints, is precisely what delivers on the promise made back in the Why Services topic, a stable address that quietly, correctly, keeps working even as the real Pods behind it come and go.

blocks.alt: The concrete mechanism finally delivering on the stability promised much earlier

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: A Pod sends traffic to a Service's virtual IP, kube-proxy transparently intercepts and redirects it to a real, currently matching backing Pod.
This entire mechanism happens invisibly to the sending Pod, it is exactly what makes a Service a genuinely stable abstraction over Pods that constantly come and go.
